title: CXMT To Leapfrog Samsung By ~2 Years, As It Gears Up To Introduce A DDR5 RDIMM Product That Leverages The 4F² Memory Cell Architecture Before Year-End
key_facts: CXMT's president, Dr. Cao Kanyu, spoke at the 4th Integrated Chip and Chiplet Conference in Shanghai about the next-generation 4F² DRAM architecture and hybrid bonding.
He said CXMT will introduce a DDR5 RDIMM product based on 4F² before the end of 2026, which Wccftech puts at around two years ahead of Samsung's roadmap for the architecture.
A post on X cited by Wccftech says Samsung plans to introduce 4F² in 2028.
4F² stacks the transistor and capacitor of each memory cell vertically; Wccftech says this can raise cell density by 30 to 50 percent and cut cell area by about 33 percent versus 6F².
Wccftech says it is quite likely CXMT's first implementation would be a partial derivative of 4F² on its new 15nm G5 DRAM process.
Wccftech says CXMT is expanding to about 300,000 wafers a month by the end of this year and is on course to overtake Micron in volume production by 2030.
An RDIMM is a server memory module with a buffer that lets operators fit more high-capacity memory sticks on one motherboard.
quote_evidence: During the speech, Dr. Kanyu declared that CXMT will introduce a DDR5 RDIMM product based on the 4F² memory cell architecture before the end of 2026, which is around two years ahead of Samsung's roadmap for the introduction of this architecture.
Just by changing the structure to 4F², DRAM makers are able to increase the cell density of each IC by 30 - 50 percent.
Even so, it is quite likely that CXMT's initial implementation would be a partial derivative of the 4F² architecture on its new 15nm G5 DRAM process.
why_it_matters_hint: If CXMT delivers, a Chinese memory maker would challenge Samsung, SK hynix and Micron on a next-generation memory design.
event_date: Speech date not stated ('recently'); Wccftech article 10 Oct 2026.
notes: Company claim relayed by one outlet; no independent confirmation and no product shipped. The speech date is not given in the article. Searches found no other outlet carrying it.
